change.describe: branch `ao-replay/9086-r2` of ao-replay-9086-r2 against a4542d6c630184148510fd43d2a3a83eb7d32b87 (merge-base a4542d6)
change.title: ao-replay/9086-r2
change.description: fix(devices): keep parked records crash-safe and listing-accurate
change.author: Prasad-D-Ware

contracts.action: Park an owned device in the same save that removes its lease (endLeaseLocked, and Open's lease replacement)
contracts.equivalent_path: finishRelease used to be the only place that parked a device, after the release finished
contracts.before_after: Before: lease removal was saved, then the parked record was saved later in finishRelease, so a daemon stop in between lost the record. Now: parkLocked runs before the same saveLocked. finishRelease still parks through the same helper, and deletes both records when a requested shutdown succeeds.
contracts.visible_effect: A simulator AO started is still powered off after a daemon restart once its session has ended, instead of running on.
contracts.failure_mode: If the shutdown in Close(shutdown=true) fails, the record stays parked, as before. If the daemon dies mid-shutdown while the session is alive, the stale parked/owned record is dropped by forgetStoppedLocked on the next Open, because the device lists as off.

contracts.action: retireParked lists per platform through ports.DevicePlatformLister, falling back to List filtered by platform, and keeps the parked/owned records until Shutdown succeeds
contracts.equivalent_path: releaseIfGone already uses ListPlatform when the provider implements it, so a failed platform listing is not taken as the device being gone
contracts.before_after: Before: List was called once. A device missing from a successful but partial list read as off and was forgotten while still running. The records were deleted before Shutdown and restored on error. Now: a failed platform is skipped for this pass. The records are deleted only after Shutdown succeeds, and releasing blocks other opens meanwhile.
contracts.visible_effect: No simulator is left running unowned after a partial simctl failure, and a stopped daemon retries the power-off.
contracts.failure_mode: A listing error is only logged at Debug and retried on the next 30s pass. The fallback listPlatform for a provider without the interface returns a nil error when List succeeds, which matches the old behaviour.

contracts.action: Open skips forgetStoppedLocked when a boot finished since before its listing (bootGen)
contracts.equivalent_path: forgetStoppedLocked previously trusted any listing taken before a concurrent boot finished
contracts.before_after: Before: a listing that showed a device off was used even if a boot of it had finished in the meantime, so it could drop ownership of a running device. Now: the generation is read before List and compared under s.mu, and nothing is dropped if a boot finished in between.
contracts.visible_effect: Prevents a running AO-booted simulator from being forgotten, and so never powered off, after a race between two opens.
contracts.failure_mode: Any boot, including a failed one or one for another device, skips the forgetting for that one Open. The next Open retries, so the delay is harmless.

summary: I found nothing to flag in either file. The change is consistent with the code it touches: the parked record is saved in the same lock hold as the lease removal, and `retireParked` drops its records only after `Shutdown` succeeds. `retireParked` also lists per platform, the same way `releaseIfGone` already does, and the `bootGen` check is read before the listing and compared under `s.mu`. The new tests exercise those paths with the existing fakes and helpers (`endableSessions`, `openBooted`, `releaseGate`, `shutdownGate`). I read the code only and did not run the tests.
